title: Discipleship and Follow-up
summary: How to help new and growing believers follow Jesus: the meaning of discipleship, Jesus' method, follow-up of new converts, one-to-one and small-group discipling, and multiplying disciple-makers.
description: Jesus did not command us to make converts but disciples. This course explains what a disciple is, how Jesus made disciples, how to follow up new believers in their first weeks, how to disciple one-to-one and in small groups, and how to train disciples who will disciple others, so that churches grow deep as well as wide.
objectives: Learn from Jesus' method of making disciples
Plan effective follow-up of new believers
outcomes: Describe marks of a disciple from Scripture
Explain selection, association and impartation in Jesus' method
Lead a discovery Bible study in a small group

modules.title: What Is a Disciple?
modules.intro: A disciple is a learner and follower of Jesus. This week we study the meaning and cost of discipleship.

lessons.title: Learner and follower
lessons.body:
The Greek word *mathetes* means a learner or apprentice. In Jesus' day a disciple followed a teacher, lived with him and became like him: "It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master" (Matthew 10:25).

Jesus called people: "Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men" (Matthew 4:19). The goal of discipleship is to become like Christ and to share in His mission.

In Acts, "disciples" is the normal name for believers (Acts 11:26). There is no separate class of 'ordinary Christians' who are not disciples. Every believer is called to follow and learn.

lessons.title: Marks of a disciple
lessons.body:
Jesus named marks of His disciples:

- **Abiding in His Word**: "If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed" (John 8:31).
- **Love for one another**: "By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another" (John 13:35).
- **Fruitfulness**: "Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples" (John 15:8).
- **Self-denial**: "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me" (Luke 9:23).

These marks grow over time. Discipleship is a lifelong journey.

lessons.title: The cost of discipleship
lessons.body:
Jesus told crowds to count the cost: "whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple" (Luke 14:33). He must come before family (14:26), possessions and self.

This is not earning salvation, which is a free gift. It is the response of those who have found a treasure worth everything (Matthew 13:44).

When discipling others, we must not hide the cost or offer an easy Christianity. Yet we also show that Jesus' "yoke is easy, and [his] burden is light" (Matthew 11:28-30). Following Him is costly and also the best life there is.

modules.title: Jesus' Method
modules.intro: Jesus spent most of His ministry training a few. This week we study how He made disciples.

lessons.title: Selection and association
lessons.body:
After a night of prayer, Jesus chose twelve from among His followers (Luke 6:12-13). He "ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach" (Mark 3:14).

Notice the order: first **with Him**, then **sent**. Jesus' main method was association: they lived, travelled, ate and ministered together. They watched Him pray, heal, teach and handle opposition.

Within the Twelve, Jesus spent extra time with Peter, James and John (Mark 9:2). Discipleship is personal and relational, not only classes and programmes.

lessons.title: Teaching, demonstration and practice
lessons.body:
Jesus taught in many ways:

- **Teaching**: the Sermon on the Mount, parables, private explanations (Mark 4:34).
- **Demonstration**: "I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done" (John 13:15).
- **Practice**: He sent the Twelve out two by two (Mark 6:7) and the Seventy (Luke 10:1).
- **Debrief**: they returned and "told him all things" (Mark 6:30), and He taught them further (Luke 10:17-20).
- **Correction**: He rebuked pride (Mark 9:33-35) and lack of faith with patience.

A simple pattern is: I do, you watch; we do together; you do, I watch; you do, someone else watches.

lessons.title: Patience and commissioning
lessons.body:
Jesus' disciples were slow to understand, often proud and sometimes faithless. Peter denied Him; all forsook Him. Yet Jesus kept loving them "unto the end" (John 13:1) and restored Peter (John 21:15-17).

Discipling requires patience. People grow slowly and fail. We must correct with gentleness (2 Timothy 2:24-25), not give up.

Finally Jesus commissioned them: "Go ye therefore, and teach all nations" (Matthew 28:19-20), and promised His presence and Spirit. The disciples became disciple-makers. The aim of discipleship is not dependence on the discipler but faithful followers who make others.

modules.title: Following Up New Believers
modules.intro: The first weeks after conversion are crucial. This week we learn how to follow up new believers.

lessons.title: Why follow-up matters
lessons.body:
New believers are like newborn babies who need milk (1 Peter 2:2), protection and care. Without follow-up many fall away, like seed on stony ground (Mark 4:16-17).

Paul and Barnabas returned to the cities where people had believed, "Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith" (Acts 14:21-22). Paul sent Timothy to Thessalonica "to establish you, and to comfort you concerning your faith" (1 Thessalonians 3:2).

Follow-up is not optional. The evangelist's work is not complete until a new believer is rooted in Christ and the church.

lessons.title: The first month
lessons.body:
A simple four-week plan, meeting weekly:

- **Week 1: Assurance of salvation**: John 5:24; 1 John 5:11-13. Help them know they are saved by grace.
- **Week 2: Bible and prayer**: Psalm 119:105; Matthew 6:9-13. Start reading a Gospel daily and praying simply.
- **Week 3: Victory over temptation and sin**: 1 Corinthians 10:13; 1 John 1:9. How to resist and how to confess.
- **Week 4: Church, baptism and witness**: Hebrews 10:25; Acts 2:41; Mark 5:19. Join a church, prepare for baptism, tell others.

Give a Bible, pray together, and listen to their questions and struggles.

lessons.title: Special situations
lessons.body:
Some new believers face particular challenges:

- **Opposition at home**: especially from families of other faiths. Teach wisdom, respect for parents, and endurance (Matthew 10:34-36; 1 Peter 4:12-16). Stay in close contact.
- **Past occult involvement**: help them renounce and destroy charms and items (Acts 19:18-19) and pray with them.
- **Addictions and broken relationships**: connect them with mature believers and, where needed, professional help.
- **Children and teenagers**: work with their parents and the church.

Match new believers with a mature discipler of the same gender for personal follow-up, with appropriate safeguards.

terms.def: Caring for and teaching new believers so they become established.

modules.title: Making Disciple-Makers
modules.intro: Discipleship multiplies when disciples disciple others. This week we study small groups, one-to-one discipling and multiplication.

lessons.title: One-to-one and small groups
lessons.body:
**One-to-one discipling**, like Paul with Timothy ("my own son in the faith", 1 Timothy 1:2), allows personal attention, accountability and honest conversation.

**Small groups** of about six to twelve, like Jesus with the Twelve, allow shared learning, prayer and mutual care. The early church met "from house to house" (Acts 2:46; 20:20).

A simple small-group meeting: share how the week went; pray; read a Bible passage together; ask what it teaches about God and people and how we will obey; and decide who each person will share with this week.

lessons.title: Discovery Bible study
lessons.body:
A **discovery Bible study** helps people learn directly from Scripture rather than only from a teacher. After reading a passage aloud and retelling it in their own words, the group asks:

1. What does this passage teach about God?
2. What does it teach about people?
3. How will I obey this?
4. Who will I share this with?

This method is simple enough for new believers to lead, and it builds obedience, not just knowledge: "be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only" (James 1:22). Mature leaders guard against error by guiding the group back to the text.

lessons.title: Multiplication
lessons.body:
"And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also" (2 Timothy 2:2).

This verse shows four generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful men, and others. If every disciple helps two others each year, multiplication outruns mere addition.

Look for people who are **faithful, available and teachable**. Give them responsibility early, and release them to lead their own groups. Churches grow healthy when every member is both being discipled and discipling others. "I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase" (1 Corinthians 3:6).

assignments.title: A discipling relationship
assignments.prompt: Meet with a newer believer weekly for a month using the follow-up plan in Week 3. Describe what you covered, how they responded, what you learned, and what you would do differently, using passages from the course.

assignments.title: A multiplying small group
assignments.prompt: Design a small group for your church or campus fellowship based on discovery Bible study. Describe the meeting pattern, the first six passages you would study, how you will train new leaders, and when and how the group will multiply.
